item.title: U.S. has done "amazing job" with Iran war, Trump says
item.description: There was no sign of the conflict ending as Iran claimed to have struck two ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Families sue Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube over deaths of 4 teens
item.description: The families of four children who died by suicide allege that using social media led to depression, anxiety and other mental health problems.

item.title: Here's how much interest a $10,000 2-year CD account will earn if opened this August
item.description: In today's economy, locking $10,000 into a 2-year CD makes sense. Here's how much interest you would earn if you do.

item.title: Lawyer for Rep. Miller's ex-wife files for restraining order amid abuse claims
item.description: The ex-wife of GOP Rep. Max Miller asked a court to issue a restraining order blocking Miller from contacting her lawyer, as the Ohio congressman faces allegations of abuse — which he denies.

item.title: 3 states would face Colorado River water cuts under federal plan
item.description: Arizona, California, and Nevada would take less water from the Colorado River under a federal proposal to stave off a crisis in the river.

item.title: Trump says he's losing faith in Iran as doubts mount about a potential peace deal
item.description: President Trump gathered his Cabinet at Camp David to discuss the wars in Iran and Ukraine, as well as other administration priorities. Mr. Trump also took questions from reporters. CBS News' Nancy Cordes has the latest.

item.title: Netflix sued for allegedly losing unreleased Nicolas Cage movie
item.description: A lawsuit alleges that a drive storing a $45 million spy film starring Nicolas Cage was "stolen right off a Netflix desk."

item.title: U.S. probing if Iran was behind cyberattack on water systems in 7 states
item.description: Malicious cyber activity affected technology at water systems in at least seven states this week, including Minnesota, leading authorities to dig into whether Iranian actors are behind the attack, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Netflix sued for allegedly losing "master copy" of unreleased Nicolas Cage movie
item.description: A U.K.-based production company and a filmmaker are suing Netflix for allegedly losing a "master copy" of an unreleased Nicolas Cage movie. CBS News' Vladimir Duthiers reports.

item.title: Bears feast on salmon at Alaska's Brooks Falls to bulk up ahead of winter
item.description: Bears are congregating in Brooks Falls, Alaska, as they attempt to fatten themselves up as much as possible before winter hibernation begins. Katmai National Park and Preserve ranger Troy Hunt explains why the burly mammals head to this river to eat as many fish as they can bear.

item.title: Full interview: Boxing legend Canelo Álvarez on motivations, love for his sport
item.description: Champion boxer Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez is renowned in Mexico and beyond for his many wins and titles. Álvarez spoke with "CBS Mornings" co-host Nate Burleson about his long boxing career and relentless hunger to fight and win.

item.title: New York sues Kalshi, alleging it enables illegal gambling
item.description: A growing number of U.S. states are seeking to crack down on prediction markets, but face pushback from federal regulators.

item.title: Trump gathers Cabinet at Camp David to discuss Iran, Ukraine and alleged fraud
item.description: President Trump brought his Cabinet to Camp David to discuss Iran, Israel, Ukraine, immigration and other priorities. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: When 'cheap' HVAC repair costs you more: How to know the work was done right
item.description: Before you celebrate the bargain you got on your HVAC repair, make sure it won't lead to a bigger bill later.

item.title: Tony Romo on leave from CBS Sports after arrest
item.description: Romo was arrested in Wisconsin last week, accused of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

item.title: Spain sends over 25,000 migrants back to Morocco from Ceuta; dozens dead
item.description: The president of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, estimated that 60,000 migrants had entered the enclave from Morocco and said that at least 34 people had died.

item.title: Latest news on Middle East after Trump says Gaza peace plan is moving along
item.description: All eyes are on Israel's response after President Trump announced that Hamas agreed to the next phase of the Gaza peace plan. CBS News' Weijia Jiang and Aaron MacLean report.

item.title: Democrats demand training info on ICE agent who killed immigrant in Maine
item.description: Two Democrats are demanding details and records about the training of an ICE officer who shot and killed a Colombian immigrant in Maine, according to a letter obtained by CBS News.

item.title: Canelo Álvarez prepares for his return to the boxing ring
item.description: Boxer Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez spoke exclusively to "CBS Mornings" about his return to the ring, building his career and his future in the sport.

item.title: Boxer Canelo Álvarez explains his relentless drive to win and break records
item.description: With over 60 wins and world titles across four weight divisions, champion boxer Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez has become an icon in Mexico. "CBS Mornings" sat down with Álvarez to learn what drives him.

item.title: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham reignites WNBA debate over trans athletes
item.description: The debate over transgender athletes has overtaken the WNBA after a co-owner of the Seattle Storm was fined for her heated exchange with fans of Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. Cunningham is known for her stance against trans athletes in women's sports.

item.title: Colin Gray, father who gave rifle to Apalachee High School shooter, sentenced to 15 years
item.description: Colin Gray, the father of the teen who was convicted of killing four in a mass shooting at Apalachee High School in Georgia, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter. Prosecutors said he ignored warning signs, giving his son an assault-style semiautomatic rifle and ammunition as a gift.

item.title: How much debt do you need before creditors will negotiate?
item.description: When it comes to settling debt, the amount you owe matters, but it's just one of the factors in the equation.

item.title: Why some women in menopause are taking testosterone to manage symptoms
item.description: Some menopausal women are taking testosterone or other forms of hormone replacement therapy in order to circumvent certain symptoms. Dr. Taraneh Shirazian explains the potential risks and benefits.

item.title: FIFA official resigns in protest of World Cup investment plan
item.description: The pressure is rising on FIFA President Gianni Infantino to ditch a $20 billion privatization plan, but soccer's governing body is doubling down and criticizing the media.

item.title: Pentagon weighs eliminating civilian tenure at military academies, draft memo says
item.description: The Pentagon is considering a sweeping remake of military higher education, including an end to civilian tenure and a "line-by-line" review of courses, according to a draft memo obtained by CBS News.

item.title: Trump says Hamas agreed to next phase of Gaza peace deal, including disarmament
item.description: President Trump said Hamas and his international "Board of Peace" have agreed on the next steps in a peace deal that includes Hamas' disarmament in the Gaza Strip.

item.title: People with disabilities fear service cuts as DOJ questions legal protections
item.description: The Department of Justice in June issued a legal opinion saying states aren't required to provide services that help people with disabilities remain in their homes.

item.title: Colorado River reservoirs hit record lows as government threatens major cuts
item.description: It's a moment of reckoning in the drought-stricken West as seven states can't agree on how to share the rapidly shrinking water supply.

item.title: The West's historic snow drought could bring water shortages, wildfires
item.description: The western United States experienced a severe snow drought this year, threatening the region's water supply and potentially setting the stage for its wildfire season.
